# Cue

> Cue is a free, open-source daily notes and to-do app for Mac and iPhone. Every day is a
> page: you open it and type, with no project, tag or priority to choose first. It works
> offline with no account, stores your notes on your own device, and has no tracking of any
> kind. Sync between your Mac and iPhone is optional and also free.

Cue is made by one person, Zach Waterfield, as a personal project, and it is his daily
driver. It is in beta and deliberately small.

## What it is

- Free. There is no paid plan, no trial and no credit card. Sync is free too.
- Open source under the MIT license: https://github.com/zlwaterfield/cue
- No account needed. Both apps are complete on their own; without an account nothing you
  write leaves your device.
- Local-first. On the Mac every note lives in one SQLite file at
  `~/Library/Application Support/Cue/cue.sqlite`, with a daily snapshot kept for 14 days.
- No tracking. No analytics, no telemetry, no ads, no cookies on the website, nothing sold.
  Your notes are never training data for an AI model.
- Fast, and measured against budgets in tests: ready to type 240 ms after launch with five
  years of notes, 1.5 ms from a keystroke to the frame, 0.5 ms to search 36,543 items.
- Keyboard-first on the Mac: Tab nests, ⌘↩ completes, ⌘D moves what’s unfinished to
  tomorrow, and ⌘K is a command palette that understands dates like “move to fri”.
- Touch-first on the iPhone: tap a bullet to make it a to-do, swipe to complete or send to
  tomorrow, long-press to drag.
- Export from the Mac at any time: Markdown, one file per day, or all notes as JSON.

## What it deliberately isn’t

Cue has no projects, tags, priorities, folders, reminders, recurring tasks, attachments,
collaboration, dashboards or AI writing your notes. Days are the only structure. If you want
a project manager or a second brain, Cue is the wrong tool and says so.

## Assistants, over MCP

Cue has no AI inside it and isn’t going to. Instead it runs an MCP server, so an assistant you
already use — Claude, ChatGPT or another — can read your days, add to-dos, check them off and
move them. An edit an assistant makes syncs to your Mac and iPhone about a second later, like
any other. It needs sync turned on, it is free, and there are five tools: `get_day`,
`find_todos`, `search`, `add_lines` and `update_lines`. None of them delete anything, and the
database refuses deletion from an assistant’s token as well. Connect at
https://www.usecue.today/mcp and disconnect at https://www.usecue.today/oauth/consent.

## Sync, and the only servers involved

Sync is optional and off until you turn it on. You only need an account if you want the same
notes on more than one device. Signing in is Sign in with Apple or a six-digit code emailed
to you; there are no passwords. Notes are then stored in a Postgres database at Supabase,
where row-level security means an account can only ever read its own rows. Turning sync off
keeps every note on your device, and deleting your account in Settings deletes it from the
server. Notes are encrypted in transit and at rest, but not end-to-end, because the server
has to read them to sync them. The only servers Cue has are that Postgres database, the
sign-in that comes with it, the MCP endpoint and the website — there is no analytics service,
no ad network and no third party watching.
